
# Nexub Design System

Nexub DS is a token-driven React design system for SaaS products. The visual language is **Calm Depth**: tonal surfaces, one accent per view, spring motion, honest numbers. **Liquid Glass** is an optional material for the floating control layer. **Marketing mode** (`data-mode="marketing"`) is the livelier look for marketing sites, on the same tokens.

Reference files (read only what the task needs):

- [references/components.md](references/components.md): every component and pattern, grouped by category. Start here.
- `references/components/<slug>.md`: props, examples, when to use and accessibility for one component. Read it before using a component you have not used yet in this session.
- [references/tokens.md](references/tokens.md): color roles, type roles, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, z-index.
- [references/react-native.md](references/react-native.md): **mobile apps** (Expo / React Native). Use `@nexub/react-native` and `@nexub/react-native/patterns` there, never `@nexub/react`.

## 1. Check the setup first

Look for `@nexub/react` in `package.json`. If it is missing, set it up:

```bash
npm install @nexub/react @nexub/patterns @nexub/themes @nexub/tokens @nexub/icons
```

```ts
// app entry or global CSS, once
import '@nexub/themes/base';   // resets + token CSS variables
import '@nexub/themes/light';
import '@nexub/themes/glass';  // only if you use Liquid Glass
```

```css
/* Tailwind 4 (Tailwind 3 is not supported from 4.0): no config file. Load the theme CSS here, in the base layer, instead of from JS */
@layer theme, base, components, utilities;
@import "@nexub/themes/base" layer(base);
@import "@nexub/themes/light" layer(base);
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@nexub/tokens/tailwind.css";
@source "../node_modules/@nexub/react/dist";
@source "../node_modules/@nexub/patterns/dist";
```

**Next.js App Router:** presentational components (Heading, Text, Container, Section, Stack, Badge, EyebrowChip, Logo, Float, Marquee and every `@nexub/marketing` section except `MarketingNav`, `PricingTable` and `FAQ`) are server components. Import per component (`@nexub/react/Button`, `@nexub/marketing/Hero`, `cn` from `@nexub/react/cn`) or set `experimental.optimizePackageImports: ['@nexub/react', '@nexub/marketing', '@nexub/icons']`, or the page ships every client component. Compound components (`Accordion.Root`, `TopNav.Root`) only work inside a `'use client'` file. To use `next/font`, import `@nexub/themes/core` (no fonts, no page backdrop) instead of `base` and name the font variables `--font-family-sans` and `--font-family-display`. With Tailwind, never also import `@nexub/react/styles.css`.

Wrap the app in `<ThemeProvider defaultTheme="system" storageKey="app-theme">` from `@nexub/react`. In server-rendered apps (Next.js), put `<ThemeScript storageKey="app-theme" />` in `<head>` and add `suppressHydrationWarning` to `<html>`. Product brands: set `data-product="leap" | "bookub" | "payub" | "founderub"` on the root. This remaps the `tertiary` role.

## 2. How to build a screen

1. **Start from a pattern.** Check the Patterns sections of `references/components.md` before you compose anything by hand.
2. **Then use components.** Use `@nexub/react` for every control, overlay, layout primitive and piece of typography. Never hand-roll a button, input, dialog, menu or table that the library already has.
3. **Then use tokens, only for the glue.** Use Tailwind utilities from the preset or v4 theme (`bg-surface-container-low`, `text-on-surface-variant`, `p-4`, `gap-6`, `rounded-shape-container`, `text-title-md`) or `var(--…)`.
4. **Never hardcode design values.** That means no hex or rgb colors, no Tailwind palette colors (`bg-blue-500`, `text-gray-600`), no arbitrary px values (`p-[13px]`), no ad-hoc shadows or gradients.

Starting points for typical SaaS screens:

| Screen | Build with |
| --- | --- |
| App frame | `AppShell` (`AppShell.Root/Header/Body/Sidebar/Main`) + `Sidebar` or `NavigationRail` + `AppHeader` or `TopNav` |
| Dashboard | `PageHeader` + a `Grid` of `StatCard` + `BarChart` / `LineChart` + `DataTable` or `Table` + `ActivityFeed` |
| Charts | `BarChart` (compare categories), `LineChart` (trend over time), `DonutChart` (parts of a whole, six slices at most), `Sparkline` (trend inside a stat or table cell). Pass `title`, `data`, `index` and `series`; colours come from the chart palette, never hex |
| List / detail | `ListDetail` + `FilterBar` + `EmptyState` |
| Settings | `SettingsLayout` / `SettingsRow` + `SettingsSection` + `FormField` |
| Sign in / sign up | `AuthCard` + `FormField` + `PasswordInput` |
| Pricing / billing | `PlanCard` + `SegmentedControl` (monthly / yearly) + `Amount` |
| Onboarding | `StepIndicator` + `CheckList` |
| Search / commands | `CommandPalette` + `KeyboardShortcut` |
| Empty, loading, error | `EmptyState`, `Skeleton`, `ErrorState`, `Toast` |
| Expressive moment (onboarding, hero, success) | `@nexub/themes/vivid` + `data-expression="vivid"` on that area, `Aurora` behind the hero. One expressive moment per screen; keep dense tables and forms Calm |
| White-label / customer brand | `<ThemeProvider seed="#hex">` (native: `<NexubNativeProvider seed>`), plus `createSeedStylesheet(seed)` from `@nexub/tokens/seed` rendered on the server so there is no flash. Never hand-pick brand hex for roles; try colours at nexub.design/foundations/theme-builder |
| Marketing / landing page | `@nexub/marketing` under `data-mode="marketing"`: `MarketingNav`, `Hero`, `LogoStrip`, `StatBand`, `FeatureSplit`, `HowItWorks`, `ProductGrid`, `TestimonialGrid`, `PricingTable`, `FAQ`, `CTABand`, `MarketingFooter` |

Money: use `Amount` and `MoneyInput`. They use tabular figures, the currency's own minor unit and a true minus sign. Icons: import from `@nexub/icons`, not `lucide-react` directly.

## 3. Calm Depth principles

1. **Content leads, chrome recedes.** Navigation is quieter than content. Remove a divider before you add one; let spacing and tone separate regions. Do: a tonal sidebar with no border, where the active item is a soft pill. Don't: a saturated brand-blue sidebar item, or a hard line around every region.
2. **Hierarchy through tone and layout, not decoration.** Surfaces step `surface` → `surface-container-*` → `surface-elevated`. Shadows are only for things that float. Product UI has no gradients, no colored icon tiles and no gradient eyebrow chips (those belong to marketing mode only).
3. **One accent, spent deliberately.** Each view gets one filled (primary) button. Everything else is `tonal`, `outlined` or `text`. Never put two filled buttons side by side.
4. **Physical, interruptible motion.** Use the spring tokens (`ease-spatial-default duration-spatial-default`), not raw durations. Exits are faster than entrances. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
5. **Honest numbers and states.** Use tabular figures in data. Hover, pressed, selected and disabled are explicit component states. Never fake a state with opacity.
6. **Accessible by construction.** Every role pair meets WCAG 2.2 AA in light, dark and high contrast, as long as you pair a role with its `on-` role. Keep visible focus, labelled controls (`FormField` + `Label`) and keyboard support. Use `VisuallyHidden` for icon-only labels.

## 4. Liquid Glass rules

- Glass is for the floating control layer only: top bars, floating toolbars, popovers, menus, sheets, dialogs. Card glass is only for surfaces over imagery or media.
- Turn it on through props: `<TopNav.Root surface="glass" scrollEdge="soft">`, `<Dialog.Content surface="glass">`, `<Button variant="glass">`.
- Never put glass on glass. Show at most three glass layers at a time. Tint only the one primary action (`data-glass-tint="primary"`).
- Never put white text on glass over an unknown background.

## 5. Marketing mode rules

- Turn it on with `data-mode="marketing"` and `@nexub/themes/marketing`. Nothing outside the attribute changes; never use it in product UI.
- Gradients in three places only: the `Hero`, the main button (`Button variant="hero"`) and the `CTABand`.
- At most one `variant="hero"` button per screen; pair it with an outlined button.
- Product accents (`Card variant="showcase" accent="payub"`, `TestimonialCard accent`) only on product-specific content.
- Motion budget: one entrance per section (`Reveal` or the hero's rise), at most two `Float`s in view, one `Marquee` plus the footer's. All of it stops under reduced motion.
- Page width `Container size="marketing"` (1280px); headlines `text-display-xl` on the hero only; one h1 per page (the `Hero` title).

## 6. UI copy

Copy is clear, direct, human and confident. Use sentence case, active voice, contractions and specific verbs ("Save changes", not "Submit"). Errors say what happened and what to do: "Your session expired. Sign in again." No "Oops", no emoji in errors, no "Please be advised".

## 7. Before you finish

- [ ] Every control comes from `@nexub/react` or `@nexub/patterns`. No deprecated component (see the index).
- [ ] There are no hex or rgb colors, Tailwind palette colors, arbitrary px values or custom shadows. Everything is a token utility or `var(--…)`.
- [ ] Every background role is paired with its `on-` role. Secondary text uses `on-surface-variant` or `on-surface-muted`.
- [ ] Each view has at most one filled button (marketing: at most one hero button).
- [ ] In Next.js, server pages import per component and use no compound component outside a `'use client'` file.
- [ ] The screen works in light and dark (`data-theme`) and at `data-contrast="high"`.
- [ ] Every input has a label. Icon-only buttons have an `aria-label`. Keyboard paths work.


---

# Tokens

Nexub DS v5.2.0. Every token is a CSS custom property from `@nexub/tokens/css` (loaded by `@nexub/themes/base`).
The Tailwind preset (`@nexub/tokens/tailwind`) maps them to utilities. Never hardcode a hex, px spacing or shadow that a token covers.

## Color roles

Roles are `light-dark()` values: they follow `data-theme` and `data-contrast` automatically. Pair every background role with its `on-` role.

| Role | Tailwind | CSS var | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | `bg-primary` / `text-primary` / `border-primary` | `--color-primary` | The one emphasised action; links |
| `on-primary` | `bg-on-primary` / `text-on-primary` / `border-on-primary` | `--color-on-primary` |  |
| `primary-container` | `bg-primary-container` / `text-primary-container` / `border-primary-container` | `--color-primary-container` |  |
| `on-primary-container` | `bg-on-primary-container` / `text-on-primary-container` / `border-on-primary-container` | `--color-on-primary-container` |  |
| `secondary` | `bg-secondary` / `text-secondary` / `border-secondary` | `--color-secondary` |  |
| `on-secondary` | `bg-on-secondary` / `text-on-secondary` / `border-on-secondary` | `--color-on-secondary` |  |
| `secondary-container` | `bg-secondary-container` / `text-secondary-container` / `border-secondary-container` | `--color-secondary-container` |  |
| `on-secondary-container` | `bg-on-secondary-container` / `text-on-secondary-container` / `border-on-secondary-container` | `--color-on-secondary-container` |  |
| `error` | `bg-error` / `text-error` / `border-error` | `--color-error` | Destructive / error |
| `on-error` | `bg-on-error` / `text-on-error` / `border-on-error` | `--color-on-error` |  |
| `error-container` | `bg-error-container` / `text-error-container` / `border-error-container` | `--color-error-container` |  |
| `on-error-container` | `bg-on-error-container` / `text-on-error-container` / `border-on-error-container` | `--color-on-error-container` |  |
| `success` | `bg-success` / `text-success` / `border-success` | `--color-success` |  |
| `on-success` | `bg-on-success` / `text-on-success` / `border-on-success` | `--color-on-success` |  |
| `success-container` | `bg-success-container` / `text-success-container` / `border-success-container` | `--color-success-container` |  |
| `on-success-container` | `bg-on-success-container` / `text-on-success-container` / `border-on-success-container` | `--color-on-success-container` |  |

| `on-warning-container` | `bg-on-warning-container` / `text-on-warning-container` / `border-on-warning-container` | `--color-on-warning-container` |  |
| `info` | `bg-info` / `text-info` / `border-info` | `--color-info` |  |
| `on-info` | `bg-on-info` / `text-on-info` / `border-on-info` | `--color-on-info` |  |
| `info-container` | `bg-info-container` / `text-info-container` / `border-info-container` | `--color-info-container` |  |
| `on-info-container` | `bg-on-info-container` / `text-on-info-container` / `border-on-info-container` | `--color-on-info-container` |  |
| `leap` | `bg-leap` / `text-leap` / `border-leap` | `--color-leap` |  |
| `on-leap` | `bg-on-leap` / `text-on-leap` / `border-on-leap` | `--color-on-leap` |  |
| `leap-container` | `bg-leap-container` / `text-leap-container` / `border-leap-container` | `--color-leap-container` |  |
| `on-leap-container` | `bg-on-leap-container` / `text-on-leap-container` / `border-on-leap-container` | `--color-on-leap-container` |  |
| `bookub` | `bg-bookub` / `text-bookub` / `border-bookub` | `--color-bookub` |  |
| `on-bookub` | `bg-on-bookub` / `text-on-bookub` / `border-on-bookub` | `--color-on-bookub` |  |
| `bookub-container` | `bg-bookub-container` / `text-bookub-container` / `border-bookub-container` | `--color-bookub-container` |  |

| `founderub-container` | `bg-founderub-container` / `text-founderub-container` / `border-founderub-container` | `--color-founderub-container` |  |
| `on-founderub-container` | `bg-on-founderub-container` / `text-on-founderub-container` / `border-on-founderub-container` | `--color-on-founderub-container` |  |
| `surface` | `bg-surface` / `text-surface` / `border-surface` | `--color-surface` | Page background |
| `surface-dim` | `bg-surface-dim` / `text-surface-dim` / `border-surface-dim` | `--color-surface-dim` |  |
| `surface-bright` | `bg-surface-bright` / `text-surface-bright` / `border-surface-bright` | `--color-surface-bright` |  |
| `surface-container-lowest` | `bg-surface-container-lowest` / `text-surface-container-lowest` / `border-surface-container-lowest` | `--color-surface-container-lowest` |  |
| `surface-container-low` | `bg-surface-container-low` / `text-surface-container-low` / `border-surface-container-low` | `--color-surface-container-low` | In-flow cards, sidebars |
| `surface-container` | `bg-surface-container` / `text-surface-container` / `border-surface-container` | `--color-surface-container` | Default container |
| `surface-container-high` | `bg-surface-container-high` / `text-surface-container-high` / `border-surface-container-high` | `--color-surface-container-high` | Pressed / neutral fills |
| `surface-container-highest` | `bg-surface-container-highest` / `text-surface-container-highest` / `border-surface-container-highest` | `--color-surface-container-highest` |  |
| `surface-elevated` | `bg-surface-elevated` / `text-surface-elevated` / `border-surface-elevated` | `--color-surface-elevated` | Floating layers: menus, popovers, dialogs |
| `on-surface` | `bg-on-surface` / `text-on-surface` / `border-on-surface` | `--color-on-surface` | Primary text |
| `on-surface-variant` | `bg-on-surface-variant` / `text-on-surface-variant` / `border-on-surface-variant` | `--color-on-surface-variant` | Secondary text |
| `on-surface-muted` | `bg-on-surface-muted` / `text-on-surface-muted` / `border-on-surface-muted` | `--color-on-surface-muted` | Tertiary text (still ≥ 4.5:1) |
| `outline` | `bg-outline` / `text-outline` / `border-outline` | `--color-outline` | Field borders, focus (≥ 3:1) |
| `outline-variant` | `bg-outline-variant` / `text-outline-variant` / `border-outline-variant` | `--color-outline-variant` | Hairlines, dividers |
| `inverse-surface` | `bg-inverse-surface` / `text-inverse-surface` / `border-inverse-surface` | `--color-inverse-surface` |  |
| `inverse-on-surface` | `bg-inverse-on-surface` / `text-inverse-on-surface` / `border-inverse-on-surface` | `--color-inverse-on-surface` |  |
| `inverse-primary` | `bg-inverse-primary` / `text-inverse-primary` / `border-inverse-primary` | `--color-inverse-primary` |  |
| `scrim` | `bg-scrim` / `text-scrim` / `border-scrim` | `--color-scrim` |  |
| `tertiary` | `bg-tertiary` / `text-tertiary` / `border-tertiary` | `--color-tertiary` | Product brand accent (remapped by data-product) |
| `on-tertiary` | `bg-on-tertiary` / `text-on-tertiary` / `border-on-tertiary` | `--color-on-tertiary` |  |
| `tertiary-container` | `bg-tertiary-container` / `text-tertiary-container` / `border-tertiary-container` | `--color-tertiary-container` |  |
| `on-tertiary-container` | `bg-on-tertiary-container` / `text-on-tertiary-container` / `border-on-tertiary-container` | `--color-on-tertiary-container` |  |

Legacy aliases (`--color-bg-*`, `--color-text-*`, `--color-border-*`, `--color-semantic-*`, raw `--color-brand-*` / `--color-accent-*` scales, `--gradient-*`) still work but must not be used in new code.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `text-display-xl` | 64px / 68px | 800 |
| `text-display-lg` | 56px / 60px | 700 |
| `text-display-md` | 44px / 48px | 700 |
| `text-display-sm` | 36px / 40px | 700 |

| `text-title-sm` | 14px / 20px | 600 |

| `text-body-sm` | 14px / 20px | 400 |

## Shape (corner radius by role)

| CSS var | Tailwind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--shape-control` | `rounded-shape-control` | 9999px |
| `--shape-field` | `rounded-shape-field` | 12px |
| `--shape-container` | `rounded-shape-container` | 16px |
| `--shape-overlay` | `rounded-shape-overlay` | 24px |
| `--shape-tooltip` | `rounded-shape-tooltip` | 8px |
| `--shape-min` | `rounded-shape-min` | 4px |

Raw radii (`rounded-sm` … `rounded-3xl`, `--radius-*`) exist; prefer the shape roles.

## Elevation

| CSS var | Tailwind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--elevation-0` | `shadow-elevation-0` | none |
| `--elevation-1` | `shadow-elevation-1` | 0 0 0 1px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.06), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.06)), 0 1px 2px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.06), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4)), 0 2px 6px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.04), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3)) |
| `--elevation-2` | `shadow-elevation-2` | 0 0 0 1px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.06), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08)), 0 2px 4px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.06), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4)), 0 8px 20px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.08), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)) |
| `--elevation-3` | `shadow-elevation-3` | 0 0 0 1px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.06), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08)), 0 4px 8px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.08), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)), 0 20px 48px light-dark(rgb(26 28 30 / 0.16), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55)) |

Shadows are only for things that float. In-flow cards use tone (`surface-container-*`) and a hairline, not a shadow.

## Motion

Use springs, not durations. Each spring has a paired easing and duration:

| Spring | Tailwind |
| --- | --- |
| `--motion-spring-spatial-fast-{easing,duration}` | `ease-spatial-fast duration-spatial-fast` |
| `--motion-spring-spatial-default-{easing,duration}` | `ease-spatial-default duration-spatial-default` |
| `--motion-spring-spatial-slow-{easing,duration}` | `ease-spatial-slow duration-spatial-slow` |
| `--motion-spring-effects-fast-{easing,duration}` | `ease-effects-fast duration-effects-fast` |
| `--motion-spring-effects-default-{easing,duration}` | `ease-effects-default duration-effects-default` |
| `--motion-spring-effects-slow-{easing,duration}` | `ease-effects-slow duration-effects-slow` |
| `--motion-spring-expressive-fast-{easing,duration}` | `ease-expressive-fast duration-expressive-fast` |
| `--motion-spring-expressive-default-{easing,duration}` | `ease-expressive-default duration-expressive-default` |
| `--motion-spring-expressive-slow-{easing,duration}` | `ease-expressive-slow duration-expressive-slow` |

`spatial` = movement and size, `effects` = color and opacity (no bounce), `expressive` = key moments only. Exits use `fast`. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Z-index

| CSS var | Tailwind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--z-hide` | `z-hide` | -1 |
| `--z-base` | `z-base` | 0 |
| `--z-raised` | `z-raised` | 10 |
| `--z-dropdown` | `z-dropdown` | 1000 |
| `--z-sticky` | `z-sticky` | 1100 |
| `--z-banner` | `z-banner` | 1200 |
| `--z-overlay` | `z-overlay` | 1300 |
| `--z-modal` | `z-modal` | 1400 |
| `--z-popover` | `z-popover` | 1500 |
| `--z-skipLink` | `z-skipLink` | 1600 |
| `--z-toast` | `z-toast` | 1700 |
| `--z-tooltip` | `z-tooltip` | 1800 |
| `--z-commandK` | `z-commandK` | 1900 |

## Breakpoints

`sm` 640px · `md` 768px · `lg` 1024px · `xl` 1280px · `2xl` 1536px

# Component index

Nexub DS v5.2.0. Open `components/<slug>.md` for props, examples and accessibility notes.
Never use a component marked deprecated.

## Components — Actions

- [Button](components/button.md) `@nexub/react`: Triggers an action or event. Supports multiple variants, sizes, and semantic tones.
- [Button Group](components/button-group.md) `@nexub/react`: Groups related buttons together with optional attachment and orientation.
- [Icon Button](components/icon-button.md) `@nexub/react`: A square button designed to hold a single icon, with an accessible label.
- [Split Button](components/split-button.md) `@nexub/react`: A primary action with related secondary actions behind a chevron, as one connected control.

## Components — AI

- [Approval Card](components/approval-card.md) `@nexub/react`: The agent asks before it acts: what will happen, then Approve or Deny.
- [Citation](components/citation.md) `@nexub/react`: Numbered source markers for running text, with a hover preview, plus SourceChip and SourceList for the sources under a reply.
- [Diff View](components/diff-view.md) `@nexub/react`: A unified diff with added and removed lines, for agent changes.
- [Message Bubble](components/message-bubble.md) `@nexub/react`: One message in a conversation. User messages sit in a bubble at the end; assistant replies run full width. MessageActions adds copy, feedback and regenerate.
- [Plan Tracker](components/plan-tracker.md) `@nexub/react`: An agent plan: ordered steps with done, active, pending or failed status.
- [Prompt Input](components/prompt-input.md) `@nexub/react`: The composer for a chat: an auto-growing text field with Send, which turns into Stop while a reply streams.
- [Streaming Text](components/streaming-text.md) `@nexub/react`: Assistant text as it arrives: new chunks fade in, text already shown stays still, and a caret marks the end.
- [Thinking Indicator](components/thinking-indicator.md) `@nexub/react`: Shows the assistant is working before the first token arrives: a morphing shape and a shimmering label.
- [Tool Call](components/tool-call.md) `@nexub/react`: One tool call: its name and status, expandable to input and output.

## Components — Avatar

- [Avatar](components/avatar.md) `@nexub/react`: Displays a user's profile picture with initials fallback.
- [Avatar Group](components/avatar-group.md) `@nexub/react`: Stacked group of avatars with overflow count.

## Components — Data Display

- [Amount](components/amount.md) `@nexub/react`: Honest money: Intl formatting, tabular numerals, the currency’s minor unit and a true minus sign.
- [Bar Chart](components/bar-chart.md) `@nexub/react`: Compare values across categories, grouped or stacked. Server-rendered SVG on the chart palette.
- [Chart Toggle](components/chart-toggle.md) `@nexub/react`: A legend whose entries switch series on and off, wrapped around any chart.
- [Data Table](components/data-table.md) `@nexub/react`: Feature-rich data table with sorting and row selection powered by TanStack Table.
- [Donut Chart](components/donut-chart.md) `@nexub/react`: Parts of a whole, with an optional total in the hole. Keep it to six slices or fewer.
- [Empty State](components/empty-state.md) `@nexub/react`: Placeholder UI shown when a list or page has no content.
- [Error State](components/error-state.md) `@nexub/react`: Full-page or section error view with retry action.
- [Funnel](components/funnel.md) `@nexub/react`: Drop-off through ordered steps, with conversion from the first step.
- [Gauge](components/gauge.md) `@nexub/react`: Progress toward a target on a 270° arc.
- [Heatmap](components/heatmap.md) `@nexub/react`: Intensity over a grid, such as activity by weekday and week, in seven sequential steps.
- [KPI Tile](components/kpi-tile.md) `@nexub/react`: A headline number with its change versus last period and a trend line.
- [Line Chart](components/line-chart.md) `@nexub/react`: Show a trend over ordered categories such as time. Server-rendered SVG on the chart palette.
- [Number Ticker](components/number-ticker.md) `@nexub/react`: A number whose digits roll to new values on the spatial spring. The first render never animates.
- [Sparkline](components/sparkline.md) `@nexub/react`: A tiny trend line with no axes, for stat cards and table cells.
- [Table](components/table.md) `@nexub/react`: Semantic HTML table with styled variants.

## Components — Disclosure

- [Accordion](components/accordion.md) `@nexub/react`: Vertically stacked list of collapsible sections.
- [Collapsible](components/collapsible.md) `@nexub/react`: Toggle visibility of content with smooth animation.
- [Scroll Area](components/scroll-area.md) `@nexub/react`: Scrollable container with custom styled scrollbars.

## Components — Dividers

- [Gradient Divider](components/gradient-divider.md) `@nexub/react`: A decorative gradient-faded horizontal rule.
- [Separator](components/separator.md) `@nexub/react`: A horizontal or vertical visual divider.

## Components — Feedback

- [Alert](components/alert.md) `@nexub/react`: Inline contextual message with optional title, icon, and dismiss action.
- [Celebrate](components/celebrate.md) `@nexub/react`: A short confetti burst for a real win, such as a first payment or finishing onboarding.
- [Spinner](components/spinner.md) `@nexub/react`: Animated loading indicator. Inherits color from context.
- [Toast](components/toast.md) `@nexub/react`: Imperative toast notifications using the toast object. Render <Toaster /> once in your layout.

## Components — Form & Input

- [Date Picker](components/date-picker.md) `@nexub/react`: Calendar date picker with text input.
- [Date Range Picker](components/date-range-picker.md) `@nexub/react`: Dual-calendar date range selector.
- [Form Field](components/form-field.md) `@nexub/react`: Wraps Label, Input, HelperText and FormError into a single accessible group.
- [Helper Text](components/helper-text.md) `@nexub/react`: Small supporting text placed beneath a form field to provide hints or validation feedback.
- [Input](components/input.md) `@nexub/react`: Text input field for forms. Supports size variants, icons, addons, and validation states.
- [Label](components/label.md) `@nexub/react`: An accessible form label that optionally shows a required asterisk and links to an input via htmlFor.
- [Money Input](components/money-input.md) `@nexub/react`: An amount field: locale-aware parsing as you type, grouped on blur, the currency symbol leading.
- [Number Input](components/number-input.md) `@nexub/react`: A numeric input with increment and decrement controls, supporting min/max clamping and step.
- [Password Input](components/password-input.md) `@nexub/react`: A password field with a built-in toggle to reveal or hide the entered value.
- [Search Input](components/search-input.md) `@nexub/react`: A text input pre-wired with a search icon and a clear button for filtering content.
- [Textarea](components/textarea.md) `@nexub/react`: A multi-line text input with configurable resize behaviour, size, and validation states.

## Components — Form Controls

- [Autocomplete](components/autocomplete.md) `@nexub/react`: Type-to-search input with matching options dropdown.
- [Checkbox](components/checkbox.md) `@nexub/react`: Binary checkbox input built on Radix UI.
- [Checkbox Card](components/checkbox-card.md) `@nexub/react`: A checkbox drawn as a whole card: title, description and optional icon. Pick any number.
- [Combobox](components/combobox.md) `@nexub/react`: Command-palette style searchable dropdown built on cmdk.
- [Multi Select](components/multi-select.md) `@nexub/react`: Pick several options as chips, with search, "+N more" and an optional create option.
- [Radio Card](components/radio-card.md) `@nexub/react`: A radio group where each option is a whole card: title, description and optional icon, one choice.
- [Radio Group](components/radio-group.md) `@nexub/react`: Group of mutually exclusive radio inputs.
- [Select](components/select.md) `@nexub/react`: Accessible dropdown select built on Radix UI. Supports groups and search.
- [Switch](components/switch.md) `@nexub/react`: Toggle control for binary on/off settings. Built on Radix UI Switch.

## Components — Forms

- [Floating Input](components/floating-input.md) `@nexub/react`: A text field whose label sits inside and floats up on focus or input. CSS only.

## Components — Inline Primitives

- [Aurora](components/aurora.md) `@nexub/react`: A decorative background of slow-drifting colour fields from the accent roles. Subtle by default, richer under data-expression="vivid".
- [Code](components/code-inline.md) `@nexub/react`: Inline code span for technical terms and short code snippets.
- [Kbd](components/kbd.md) `@nexub/react`: Keyboard key display — renders a styled <kbd> element.
- [Link](components/link.md) `@nexub/react`: Styled anchor link with variant and external support.
- [Text Gradient](components/text-gradient.md) `@nexub/react`: Renders text with a brand gradient fill.

## Components — Interactive

- [Rating](components/rating.md) `@nexub/react`: Star rating input, supports controlled and read-only modes.
- [Segmented Control](components/segmented-control.md) `@nexub/react`: Tab-style control for mutually exclusive selections.
- [Slider](components/slider.md) `@nexub/react`: Range slider built on Radix UI Slider.
- [Toggle](components/toggle.md) `@nexub/react`: Pressable toggle button built on Radix UI Toggle.
- [Toggle Group](components/toggle-group.md) `@nexub/react`: Group of toggle buttons where one or many can be active.

## Components — Labels & Badges

- [Badge](components/badge.md) `@nexub/react`: Small status indicator or label. Communicates state, category, or count.
- [Chip](components/chip.md) `@nexub/react`: Compact label chip, optionally dismissible.
- [Eyebrow Chip](components/eyebrow-chip.md) `@nexub/react`: A compact eyebrow label, typically used above headings.
- [Filter Chip](components/filter-chip.md) `@nexub/react`: Interactive chip for filtering, supports selected/unselected state.

## Components — Layout

- [Box](components/box.md) `@nexub/react`: Generic container primitive with style token props.
- [Card](components/card.md) `@nexub/react`: Surface container for grouping related content. Supports flat, surface, and interactive variants.
- [Flex](components/flex.md) `@nexub/react`: Flexbox layout primitive.
- [Grid](components/grid.md) `@nexub/react`: CSS Grid layout primitive.
- [Media Card](components/media-card.md) `@nexub/react`: An image card with a glass caption over a soft scrim. With `href`, the whole card is one link.
- [Stack](components/stack.md) `@nexub/react`: Vertical stack layout with configurable gap.

## Components — Loading States

- [Progress](components/progress.md) `@nexub/react`: Horizontal progress bar with optional tone and animation.
- [Skeleton](components/skeleton.md) `@nexub/react`: Placeholder loading animation that mimics content layout.

## Components — Motion

- [Collapse](components/motion-collapse.md) `@nexub/react`: Expands and collapses content along the block axis.
- [Fade](components/motion-fade.md) `@nexub/react`: Animates opacity between 0 and 1 based on the `in` prop.
- [Float](components/motion-float.md) `@nexub/react`: Gently bobs its content (floating cards over a hero visual), in marketing mode. Server component; still under reduced motion.
- [Marquee](components/motion-marquee.md) `@nexub/react`: A row that scrolls sideways forever (logo strips, tool lists), in marketing mode. Pauses on hover and while focus is inside, stands still under reduced motion; the repeated copy is hidden from assistive tech and can’t be focused. Server component.
- [Reveal](components/motion-reveal.md) `@nexub/react`: Fades its content up as it scrolls into view, in marketing mode. CSS scroll-driven where supported, an IntersectionObserver elsewhere; content on screen at load, and every visitor without JS or with reduced motion, just sees it.
- [Scale](components/motion-scale.md) `@nexub/react`: Scales content in/out from its center.
- [Slide](components/motion-slide.md) `@nexub/react`: Slides content in from a direction based on the `in` prop.
- [Scroll Progress](components/scroll-progress.md) `@nexub/react`: A thin bar along the top that fills as the page scrolls. CSS only.
- [Shared Element](components/shared-element.md) `@nexub/react`: Morphs the same element between two states or pages inside a view transition.

## Components — Navigation

- [Breadcrumb](components/breadcrumb.md) `@nexub/react`: Hierarchical navigation trail showing page location.
- [Navigation Rail](components/navigation-rail.md) `@nexub/react`: Navigation for medium-width windows: icons over labels, with an active pill behind the icon.
- [Pagination](components/pagination.md) `@nexub/react`: Page navigation control with prev/next and page number buttons.
- [Tabs](components/tabs.md) `@nexub/react`: Layered content panels switched by tab triggers. Built on Radix UI Tabs.

## Components — Overlays

- [Alert Dialog](components/alert-dialog.md) `@nexub/react`: Confirmation dialog that requires an explicit user action before proceeding.
- [Dialog](components/dialog.md) `@nexub/react`: Modal dialog built on Radix UI. Fully accessible with focus trapping and ARIA roles.
- [Drawer](components/drawer.md) `@nexub/react`: Slide-in panel from any edge of the screen.
- [Hover Card](components/hover-card.md) `@nexub/react`: Rich tooltip card revealed on hover.
- [Popover](components/popover.md) `@nexub/react`: Floating content panel anchored to a trigger element.
- [Sheet](components/sheet.md) `@nexub/react`: Alias for Drawer — slide-in sheet panel.
- [Tooltip](components/tooltip.md) `@nexub/react`: Floating label that appears on hover. Built on Radix UI Tooltip.

## Components — Typography

- [Heading](components/heading.md) `@nexub/react`: Semantic heading component with size, weight, and tone control.
- [Text](components/text.md) `@nexub/react`: Paragraph text component with size, tone, and weight variants.

## Marketing — Marketing

- [ProductGrid](components/product-grid.md) `@nexub/marketing`: Product cards in a grid; each card is one link with the product's accent. Server component.

- [StatBand](components/stat-band.md) `@nexub/marketing`: A band of headline numbers that count up as they scroll into view. StatBandItem is named apart from the StatCard pattern. Server component.
- [TestimonialGrid](components/testimonial-grid.md) `@nexub/marketing`: Customer quotes in product-coloured cards, with an optional star rating. Server component.

These exist; read their TypeScript props in `node_modules/<package>/dist/index.d.ts`.

- `@nexub/react`: AgentKit, AppShell, AspectRatio, Chart, CheckList, Code, CommandPalette, Container, ContextMenu, CountryBadge, DropdownMenu, FileUpload, Flag, FormError, KeyboardShortcut, Logo, Menubar, Motion, NavigationMenu, NexubProvider, PageHeader, Section, Sidebar, ThemeProvider, Toolbar, TopNav, VisuallyHidden

# Accordion

Vertically stacked list of collapsible sections.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Disclosure · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Accordion } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/accordion

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Accordion.Root type` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | Whether one or multiple items can be open at the same time. |
| `Accordion.Root collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | When type is "single", allows the open item to be collapsed by clicking it again. |
| `Accordion.Root defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | The item(s) open by default (uncontrolled). |
| `Accordion.Root value` | `string \| string[]` |  | Controlled open item(s). |
| `Accordion.Root onValueChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` |  | Callback fired when the open state changes. |
| `Accordion.Root disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables all items in the accordion. |
| `Accordion.Item value` (required) | `string` |  | Unique identifier for the item. |
| `Accordion.Item disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables this specific item. |
| `Accordion.Trigger asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Merges props onto the immediate child element. |
| `Accordion.Content forceMount` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps content in the DOM even when collapsed. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Accordion, Code } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-[480px]">
      <Accordion.Root type="single" collapsible>
        <Accordion.Item value="a">
          <Accordion.Trigger>What is Nexub?</Accordion.Trigger>
          <Accordion.Content>A design system for ambitious SaaS teams, built on tokens and accessibility.</Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item value="b">
          <Accordion.Trigger>How do I install?</Accordion.Trigger>
          <Accordion.Content>Run: <Code>pnpm add @nexub/react</Code></Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item value="c">
          <Accordion.Trigger>Is it open source?</Accordion.Trigger>
          <Accordion.Content>Yes — MIT licensed and free to use.</Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Multiple

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-[480px]">
      <Accordion.Root type="multiple">
        <Accordion.Item value="x">
          <Accordion.Trigger>Section A</Accordion.Trigger>
          <Accordion.Content>Content for section A — stays open when B is opened.</Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item value="y">
          <Accordion.Trigger>Section B</Accordion.Trigger>
          <Accordion.Content>Content for section B — multiple can be open at once.</Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Alert Dialog

Confirmation dialog that requires an explicit user action before proceeding.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Overlays · Status: stable
- Import: `import { AlertDialog } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/alert-dialog

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog.Root` | `compound` |  | Root provider component that manages open state. |
| `AlertDialog.Trigger` | `compound` |  | Element that opens the dialog on interaction. |
| `AlertDialog.Portal` | `compound` |  | Portals the overlay and content into the document body. |
| `AlertDialog.Overlay` | `compound` |  | Dimmed backdrop rendered behind the content. |
| `AlertDialog.Content` | `compound` |  | The dialog panel containing title, description, and actions. |
| `AlertDialog.Title` | `compound` |  | Accessible title announced to screen readers. |
| `AlertDialog.Description` | `compound` |  | Supporting description text for the dialog. |
| `AlertDialog.Action` | `compound` |  | Confirms the destructive or affirmative action and closes the dialog. |
| `AlertDialog.Cancel` | `compound` |  | Cancels the action and closes the dialog. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button, AlertDialog } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="destructive" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Delete account</Button>
      <AlertDialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <AlertDialog.Portal>
          <AlertDialog.Overlay />
          <AlertDialog.Content>
            <AlertDialog.Title>Are you absolutely sure?</AlertDialog.Title>
            <AlertDialog.Description>
              This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove all your data.
            </AlertDialog.Description>
            <div className="flex gap-2 justify-end mt-6">
              <AlertDialog.Cancel asChild><Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button></AlertDialog.Cancel>
              <AlertDialog.Action asChild><Button variant="destructive">Yes, delete</Button></AlertDialog.Action>
            </div>
          </AlertDialog.Content>
        </AlertDialog.Portal>
      </AlertDialog.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

# Alert

Inline contextual message with optional title, icon, and dismiss action.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Feedback · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Alert } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/alert

## When to use

- Communicating system status, errors, or success after an action
- Showing inline validation feedback inside a form
- Warning the user about a potentially risky operation
- Providing contextual information relevant to the current page

## When not to use

- Transient messages — use Toast for ephemeral notifications
- Blocking the user for a required decision — use AlertDialog
- Marketing or promotional messaging
- Replacing empty states — use EmptyState instead

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | Semantic colour tone of the alert. |
| `title` | `string` |  | Bold title rendered at the top of the alert. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Custom icon rendered to the left of the content. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | Action element (e.g. a button) rendered beside the content. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` |  | When provided, renders a close button that calls this handler. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return <Alert tone="info" title="Heads up">Your trial expires in 3 days.</Alert>;
}
```

## Example: Tones

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 items-start w-full max-w-[480px]">
      <Alert tone="info" title="Info">Informational message.</Alert>
      <Alert tone="success" title="Success">Operation completed successfully.</Alert>
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Warning">Something needs your attention.</Alert>
      <Alert tone="danger" title="Error">Something went wrong.</Alert>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Dismissible

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-[480px]">
      <Alert tone="success" title="Saved" onClose={() => {}}>Your changes have been saved.</Alert>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Amount

Honest money: Intl formatting, tabular numerals, the currency’s minor unit and a true minus sign.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Data Display · Status: beta
- Import: `import { Amount } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/amount

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `number` |  | The amount. |
| `currency` (required) | `string` |  | ISO 4217 code, e.g. "USD". |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale. Defaults to the user's. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'display'` | `'md'` | `display` is a hero figure with a quieter symbol and minor units. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'auto'` | `'neutral'` | `auto` colours gains success and losses error. |
| `signDisplay` | `Intl signDisplay` |  | e.g. 'exceptZero' to show + on gains. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `false` | Roll the digits to new values (NumberTicker). The first render never animates. |

## Example: Display

```tsx
import { Amount } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return <Amount value={128450.75} currency="USD" size="display" />;
}
```

## Example: Gains and losses

```tsx
import { Amount } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-4">
      <Amount value={312.4} currency="USD" tone="auto" signDisplay="exceptZero" />
      <Amount value={-89.99} currency="USD" tone="auto" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Related: [money-input](money-input.md), [number-ticker](number-ticker.md)

# Aurora

A decorative background of slow-drifting colour fields from the accent roles. Subtle by default, richer under data-expression="vivid".

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Inline Primitives · Status: beta
- Import: `import { Aurora } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/aurora

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Shape it to its container, e.g. `rounded-shape-container`. The parent needs `position: relative` and `isolate` so the aurora stays behind the content. |

## Example: Behind a hero

```tsx
import { Aurora, Button, EyebrowChip } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="relative isolate flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-4 overflow-hidden rounded-shape-container px-6 py-14 text-center">
      <Aurora />
      <EyebrowChip>New</EyebrowChip>
      <h3 className="m-0 text-headline-md text-[var(--color-on-surface)]">Your money, at a glance</h3>
      <p className="m-0 max-w-[40ch] text-body-md text-[var(--color-on-surface)]">The colour follows your brand, theme and dark mode.</p>
      <Button>Get started</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Decorative: the whole layer is `aria-hidden`.
- The fields stop drifting under reduced motion and the layer is hidden in forced-colours mode.

Related: [text-gradient](text-gradient.md)

# Autocomplete

Type-to-search input with matching options dropdown.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form Controls · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Autocomplete } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/autocomplete

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (required) | `{ value: string; label: string }[]` |  | Array of options available for selection. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The controlled selected value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Callback fired when the selected value changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Placeholder text shown in the input when empty. |
| `emptyText` | `string` |  | Text shown when no options match the current search query. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Skeleton rows while options are being fetched (5.2); "Loading" is announced. |
| `inputValue` | `string` |  | Controlled input text (5.1). |
| `onInputChange` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called as the user types, so you can fetch options (5.1). When set, options are shown as given, without built-in filtering. |
| `mode` | `'inline' \| 'popover'` | `'inline'` | Popover (5.2): a field whose list opens below it while typing. Inline keeps the list always visible; it stays the default until 6.0. |
| `onCreate` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Adds a "Create “text”" option when the text matches no option (5.2). |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the field when it has no visible label. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-[260px]">
      <Autocomplete
        options={[
          { value: 'react', label: 'React' },
          { value: 'vue', label: 'Vue' },
          { value: 'angular', label: 'Angular' },
          { value: 'svelte', label: 'Svelte' },
        ]}
        placeholder="Search framework…"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: With loading state

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-[260px]">
      <Autocomplete options={[]} loading placeholder="Loading options…" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Custom empty text

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-[260px]">
      <Autocomplete
        options={[
          { value: 'nexub', label: 'Nexub' },
          { value: 'acme', label: 'Acme Corp' },
        ]}
        placeholder="Search company…"
        emptyText="No companies found. Try a different search."
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Popover, fetch as you type

`mode="popover"` with `onInputChange`: the app filters, the list shows skeleton rows while loading.

```tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { Autocomplete } from '@nexub/react';

const all = ['Amsterdam', 'Berlin', 'Lisbon', 'London', 'Madrid', 'Paris', 'Singapore', 'Tokyo'];

// Fetch-as-you-type: onInputChange turns built-in filtering off.
export default function Example() {
  const [query, setQuery] = React.useState('');
  const [loading, setLoading] = React.useState(false);
  const [options, setOptions] = React.useState(all.map((c) => ({ value: c, label: c })));
  React.useEffect(() => {
    setLoading(true);
    const t = setTimeout(() => {
      const q = query.toLowerCase();
      setOptions(all.filter((c) => c.toLowerCase().includes(q)).map((c) => ({ value: c, label: c })));
      setLoading(false);
    }, 300);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [query]);
  return (
    <div className="w-[280px]">
      <Autocomplete
        mode="popover"
        aria-label="City"
        placeholder="Search cities…"
        options={options}
        loading={loading}
        onInputChange={setQuery}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Avatar

Displays a user's profile picture with initials fallback.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Avatar · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Avatar } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/avatar

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` |  | URL of the profile image. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Full name used to generate initials when no image is provided. |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Controls avatar dimensions. |
| `badge` | `boolean` |  | Shows a status badge on the avatar. |
| `badgeColor` | `string` |  | Colour of the status badge. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` |  | Custom fallback rendered when the image fails to load and no name is provided. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
```

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {

      {(['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const).map((s) => (

    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
```

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {

    <div className="flex gap-3 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Avatar name="Online" badge badgeColor="var(--color-success)" />
      <Avatar name="Away" badge badgeColor="var(--color-warning)" />
```

# Badge

Small status indicator or label. Communicates state, category, or count.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Labels & Badges · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Badge } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/badge

## When to use

- Labelling a status, category, or tag on an item
- Showing a count or numeric indicator alongside an element
- Highlighting new, featured, or updated content
- Communicating a stage in a workflow (draft, published, archived)

## When not to use

- Interactive filtering — use FilterChip or Chip instead
- Long text labels that exceed 2–3 words
- Critical alerts requiring user action — use Alert or Toast
- Replacing a button — badges are non-interactive by design

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'soft' \| 'outline'` | `'solid'` | Visual fill style. |
| `tone` | `'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'neutral'` | `'neutral'` | Semantic color tone. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Badge size. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon or dot rendered before the label. |

## Example: Tones

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
      <Badge tone="danger">Error</Badge>
      <Badge tone="warning">Warning</Badge>
      <Badge tone="info">Info</Badge>
      <Badge tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Variants

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Badge variant="solid" tone="success">Solid</Badge>
      <Badge variant="soft" tone="info">Soft</Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline" tone="warning">Outline</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: With leading dot

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      {(['success', 'danger', 'warning'] as const).map((t) => (
        <Badge key={t} tone={t} leadingIcon={<span className="w-[6px] h-[6px] rounded-full bg-current inline-block" />}>
          {t === 'success' ? 'Online' : t === 'danger' ? 'Offline' : 'Away'}
        </Badge>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: status (when conveying live state)
- `—`: Badges are non-interactive and have no keyboard handlers.
- Skipped in tab order. Decorative — never trap focus on a Badge.
- Reads as inline text. For live status changes, wrap in an element with `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`.
- For interactive equivalents (filtering, dismissing) reach for `Chip` or `FilterChip`.

Related: [chip](chip.md)


---

# Bar Chart

Compare values across categories, grouped or stacked. Server-rendered SVG on the chart palette.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Data Display · Status: beta
- Import: `import { BarChart } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/bar-chart

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | Accessible name of the chart and caption of its data table. |
| `data` (required) | `T[]` |  | One row per category, in order. |
| `index` (required) | `keyof T` |  | Key of the category label in each row (the x axis). |
| `series` (required) | `ChartSeries[]` |  | `{ key, label?, color? }` per series. `color` is 1–8 from the categorical chart palette; defaults to the series position. |
| `valueFormat` | `(value: number) => string` |  | Formats axis labels, hover text and the data table. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Plot height: 8, 12 or 16rem. |
| `legend` | `boolean` |  | Show the legend. Defaults to on for more than one series. |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | `false` | One bar per category with the series stacked. |

## Example: Grouped

```tsx
import { BarChart } from '@nexub/react';

const data = [
  { month: 'May', thisYear: 42, lastYear: 35 },
  { month: 'Jun', thisYear: 48, lastYear: 37 },
  { month: 'Jul', thisYear: 45, lastYear: 40 },
  { month: 'Aug', thisYear: 56, lastYear: 41 },
  { month: 'Sep', thisYear: 61, lastYear: 47 },
  { month: 'Oct', thisYear: 68, lastYear: 50 },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      className="w-full"
      title="Revenue by month"
      data={data}
      index="month"
      series={[{ key: 'thisYear', label: '2026' }, { key: 'lastYear', label: '2025' }]}
      valueFormat={(v) => `$${v}k`}
    />
  );
}
```

## Example: Stacked

```tsx
import { BarChart } from '@nexub/react';

const data = [
  { quarter: 'Q1', web: 120, ios: 80, android: 60 },
  { quarter: 'Q2', web: 140, ios: 95, android: 72 },
  { quarter: 'Q3', web: 150, ios: 110, android: 90 },
  { quarter: 'Q4', web: 170, ios: 128, android: 101 },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      stacked
      className="w-full"
      title="Signups by platform"
      data={data}
      index="quarter"
      series={[{ key: 'web', label: 'Web' }, { key: 'ios', label: 'iOS' }, { key: 'android', label: 'Android' }]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- The chart is a `figure` named by `title`. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table carries every value.
- Colour is never the only cue: the legend and table name each series. Past six series, label directly or group the rest as "Other".

Related: [line-chart](line-chart.md), [donut-chart](donut-chart.md), [sparkline](sparkline.md)

# Breadcrumb

Hierarchical navigation trail showing page location.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Navigation · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/breadcrumb

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Breadcrumb.Root aria-label` | `string` | `'breadcrumb'` | Accessible label for the nav landmark. |
| `Breadcrumb.Link href` | `string` |  | URL the breadcrumb link navigates to. |
| `Breadcrumb.Link asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Merges props onto the immediate child element, useful for router Link components. |
| `Breadcrumb.Trail items` (required) | `{ label: ReactNode; href?: string }[]` |  | The whole trail from data (5.1), root first; the last item is the current page. |
| `Breadcrumb.Trail maxItems` | `number` | `4` | Longer trails keep the first item and the last `maxItems - 1`, and move the rest into a "More" menu. |
| `Breadcrumb.Separator children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Custom separator element. Defaults to a chevron icon. |
| `Breadcrumb.Ellipsis aria-label` | `string` | `'More'` | Accessible label for the ellipsis element used to collapse long trails. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb.Root>
      <Breadcrumb.List>
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Link href="/">Home</Breadcrumb.Link></Breadcrumb.Item>
        <Breadcrumb.Separator />
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Link href="/components">Components</Breadcrumb.Link></Breadcrumb.Item>
        <Breadcrumb.Separator />
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Page>Button</Breadcrumb.Page></Breadcrumb.Item>
      </Breadcrumb.List>
    </Breadcrumb.Root>
  );
}
```

## Example: With ellipsis

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb.Root>
      <Breadcrumb.List>
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Link href="/">Home</Breadcrumb.Link></Breadcrumb.Item>
        <Breadcrumb.Separator />
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Ellipsis /></Breadcrumb.Item>
        <Breadcrumb.Separator />
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Link href="/components/navigation">Navigation</Breadcrumb.Link></Breadcrumb.Item>
        <Breadcrumb.Separator />
        <Breadcrumb.Item><Breadcrumb.Page>Breadcrumb</Breadcrumb.Page></Breadcrumb.Item>
      </Breadcrumb.List>
    </Breadcrumb.Root>
  );
}
```

## Example: Auto-collapse

Breadcrumb.Trail moves the middle of a long path into a menu.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb.Trail
      maxItems={3}
      items={[
        { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
        { label: 'Acme', href: '/' },
        { label: 'Billing', href: '/' },
        { label: 'Invoices', href: '/' },
        { label: 'INV-2041' },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

# Button Group

Groups related buttons together with optional attachment and orientation.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Actions · Status: stable
- Import: `import { ButtonGroup } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/button-group

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Lays out child buttons horizontally or vertically. |
| `attached` | `boolean` | `false` | Removes gap and merges borders between adjacent buttons. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup, Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Example: Attached

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup, Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup attached>
      <Button variant="outline">Left</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Center</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Right</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Example: Vertical

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup, Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup orientation="vertical">
      <Button variant="outline">Option A</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Option B</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Option C</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```


---

# Button

Triggers an action or event. Supports multiple variants, sizes, and semantic tones.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Actions · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Button } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/button

## When to use

- Triggering a primary or secondary action (submit, save, confirm)
- Navigating users to another page or step in a flow
- Opening a dialog, drawer, or modal overlay
- Destructive actions that need a visible, labelled control

## When not to use

- Inline text navigation — use a Link instead
- Icon-only controls — use IconButton for touch target compliance
- Selecting among multiple options — use ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl
- Passive information display with no action

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'filled' \| 'tonal' \| 'outlined' \| 'text' \| 'glass' \| 'hero' \| 'subtle' \| 'link' \| 'destructive' \| 'accent'` | `'primary'` | Visual style of the button. `hero` is the marketing-mode main button (gradient, glow, spring lift): a filled button outside `data-mode="marketing"`; one per screen. Legacy aliases still work: primary = filled, secondary = tonal, outline = outlined, ghost = text. |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Control height and padding. |
| `status` | `'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'success' \| 'error'` | `'idle'` | Async feedback (beta, 1.7.0). `loading` shows a spinner and blocks clicks but keeps focus; `success` draws a check; `error` shakes once. The label stays in flow, so the width holds. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Alias for `status="loading"`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `'Loading'` | Announced when `status` becomes `loading`. |
| `successLabel` | `string` | `'Done'` | Announced on `success`. When set, it also replaces the visible label (with a check) instead of showing the check alone. |
| `errorLabel` | `string` | `'Something went wrong'` | Announced on `error`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the button. |
| `magnetic` | `boolean` | `false` | 4.3: drifts a few pixels toward the pointer on hover. For one key action per screen. Off for touch and reduced motion. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches the button to fill its container. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon rendered before the label. |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon rendered after the label. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | Semantic colour tone — overrides the variant colour with a semantic palette. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Merges props onto the immediate child element (Radix Slot). `status` and `loading` have no effect with `asChild`. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Click me</Button>;
}
```

## Example: Variants

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Button variant="primary">Primary</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Outline</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
      <Button variant="subtle">Subtle</Button>
      <Button variant="link">Link</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Sizes

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Button size="xs" variant="primary">XSmall</Button>
      <Button size="sm" variant="primary">Small</Button>
      <Button size="md" variant="primary">Medium</Button>
      <Button size="lg" variant="primary">Large</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: States

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2 flex-wrap items-center justify-center">
      <Button variant="primary" loading>Loading</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" disabled>Disabled</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Async

Drive `status` from the request. Each click here moves to the next status.

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { type ButtonStatus, Button } from '@nexub/react';

const NEXT_STATUS: Record<ButtonStatus, ButtonStatus> = { idle: 'loading', loading: 'success', success: 'error', error: 'idle' };

export default function Example() {
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState<ButtonStatus>('idle');
  // Clicks are ignored while loading, so loading moves on by itself.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (status !== 'loading') return;
    const t = setTimeout(() => setStatus('success'), 1200);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [status]);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 items-start">
      <Button status={status} loadingLabel="Saving" successLabel="Saved" errorLabel="Couldn't save" onClick={() => setStatus(NEXT_STATUS[status])}>
        Save
      </Button>
      <span className="text-body-sm text-[var(--color-on-surface-variant)]">status: {status}</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Hero (marketing mode)

Inside `data-mode="marketing"` with `@nexub/themes/marketing` loaded. The focus ring sits outside the gradient.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';
import { ArrowRight } from '@nexub/icons';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div data-mode="marketing" className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="hero" size="lg" trailingIcon={<ArrowRight size={16} />}>Start free</Button>
      <Button variant="outlined" size="lg">Book a demo</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Magnetic

`magnetic` (4.3): drifts toward the pointer. Use it for one key action per screen.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return <Button magnetic size="lg">Start free trial</Button>;
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: button
- `Space`: Activates the focused button.
- `Enter`: Activates the focused button.
- `Tab`: Moves focus to the button in document order.
- Receives focus in document order; `disabled` removes it from the tab sequence.
- Visible focus ring uses `--color-border-focus` and meets WCAG 2.4.7 contrast.
- Announces the visible label plus the implicit "button" role.
- While loading the button sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`), so focus stays on it and clicks are ignored.
- A button with `status` or `loading` renders a polite `role="status"` region next to it that announces `loadingLabel`, `successLabel` or `errorLabel` as the status changes.
- Pair icon-only triggers with `IconButton` for a 44×44 touch target.

Related: [icon-button](icon-button.md), [button-group](button-group.md), [link](link.md)


---

# Card

Surface container for grouping related content. Supports flat, surface, and interactive variants.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Layout · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Card } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/card

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'flat' \| 'surface' \| 'interactive' \| 'showcase'` | `'flat'` | `interactive` lifts 2px on hover (spatial spring, elevation 1 → 2), sinks to 0.99 on press and adds a state layer. Use it for cards that are links or buttons. `showcase` is the marketing-mode card (24px corners, soft shadow, hover lift); a flat card outside `data-mode="marketing"`. |
| `accent` | `'leap' \| 'bookub' \| 'payub' \| 'founderub'` |  | With `variant="showcase"`: a product-coloured top edge and tint in marketing mode. Sets `data-product` on the card. Only for product-specific content. |
| `effect` | `'none' \| 'sheen' \| 'tilt'` | `'none'` | Opt-in. `sheen` is a soft light that follows the pointer, with a brighter rim near the edge. `tilt` (4.3) also leans the card toward the pointer in 3D. Off for touch, reduced motion and reduced transparency. |
| `tone` | `ToneValue` | `undefined` | Applies a semantic left-border accent. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Merges props onto the immediate child element. |
| `surface` | `'solid' \| 'glass'` | `'solid'` | Liquid-glass material treatment — see Foundations → Materials. |
| `CardLink` | `AnchorHTMLAttributes & { asChild?: boolean }` |  | Put it around the card title to make the whole card one link. Its ::after covers the card and the card shows the focus ring. Give other controls inside the card `relative z-[1]`. Use `asChild` for a router link. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
import { Card, Text } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-[280px]">
      <Card>
        <div className="font-semibold mb-1 text-[var(--color-on-surface)]">Card title</div>
        <Text size="body-sm" tone="muted">Cards group related content on a raised surface.</Text>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Variants

```tsx
import { Card, Text } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5 items-start w-[280px]">
      <Card variant="flat"><Text size="body-sm">Flat</Text></Card>
      <Card variant="surface"><Text size="body-sm">Surface</Text></Card>
      <Card variant="interactive"><Text size="body-sm">Interactive</Text></Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Card link

The whole card is one link named by its title. The button sits above the link with `relative z-[1]`.

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Card, Heading, CardLink, Text, Button } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  const [starred, setStarred] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="w-[280px]">
      <Card variant="interactive" className="p-4">
        <Heading level={3} size="h5">
          <CardLink href="#">Atlas</CardLink>
        </Heading>
        <Text size="body-sm" tone="muted">Updated 2 hours ago</Text>
        <Button size="sm" variant="text" className="relative z-[1] mt-2" onClick={() => setStarred((v) => !v)}>
          {starred ? 'Starred' : 'Star'}
        </Button>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Sheen

Move the pointer over the card.

```tsx
import { Card, Heading, Text } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="w-[280px]">
      <Card variant="surface" effect="sheen" className="p-6">
        <Heading level={3} size="h5">Pro</Heading>
        <Text size="body-sm" tone="muted">Everything in Team, plus audit logs.</Text>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Showcase (marketing mode)

Product accents on showcase cards, inside `data-mode="marketing"`.

```tsx
import { Card } from '@nexub/react';

const products = [
  { accent: 'payub', name: 'Payub', line: 'Payroll and HR' },
  { accent: 'bookub', name: 'Bookub', line: 'Bookkeeping' },
] as const;

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div data-mode="marketing" className="grid w-full gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2">
      {products.map((p) => (
        <Card key={p.name} variant="showcase" accent={p.accent} className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-6">
          <h3 className="m-0 text-title-lg">{p.name}</h3>
          <p className="m-0 text-body-md text-[var(--color-on-surface-variant)]">{p.line}</p>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Tilt

`effect="tilt"` (4.3): the card leans toward the pointer and the sheen catches the light. Hover with a mouse.

```tsx
import { Card } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full grid-cols-2 gap-4">
      {['Revenue', 'Customers'].map((t) => (
        <Card key={t} variant="interactive" effect="tilt" className="p-6">
          <p className="m-0 text-label-md text-[var(--color-on-surface-variant)]">{t}</p>
          <p className="m-0 text-title-lg">{t === 'Revenue' ? '$68,420' : '1,204'}</p>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: region (when used as a landmark)
- `Tab`: Focuses interactive children. The card itself is never focusable; with a CardLink, the link is.
- With a CardLink inside, the focus ring is drawn on the card, not around the title.
- Prefer CardLink over wrapping the whole card in `<a>`: the link’s accessible name stays the title instead of every word on the card.
- Group related content with a heading inside the Card so AT users can navigate by heading level.

Related: [media-card](media-card.md), [radio-card](radio-card.md), [alert](alert.md)

# Celebrate

A short confetti burst for a real win, such as a first payment or finishing onboarding.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Feedback · Status: beta
- Import: `import { Celebrate } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/celebrate

## When to use

- A rare, real win the user worked for: first payment received, onboarding finished, a goal reached.

## When not to use

- Routine saves or every success; use the Button success state or a Toast.
- As the only feedback: say what happened in text too.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` (required) | `boolean` |  | Bursts each time this goes from false to true. |
| `count` | `number` | `28` | Number of pieces. |

## Example: On a win

```tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { Button, Celebrate } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  const [paid, setPaid] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="relative flex flex-col items-center gap-3 py-10">
      <Celebrate active={paid} />
      <Button magnetic status={paid ? 'success' : 'idle'} successLabel="Paid" onClick={() => setPaid((p) => !p)}>
        Pay $1,250
      </Button>
      <p role="status" className="m-0 min-h-5 text-body-sm text-[var(--color-on-surface-variant)]">{paid ? 'Payment sent. Your first one!' : ''}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Decorative (`aria-hidden`). Announce the win in text, for example in a Toast or a status message.
- Hidden under reduced motion.

Related: [toast](toast.md), [button](button.md)


---

# Chart Toggle

A legend whose entries switch series on and off, wrapped around any chart.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Data Display · Status: beta
- Import: `import { ChartToggle } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/chart-toggle

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` (required) | `ChartSeries[]` |  | The same series the chart takes. |
| `children` (required) | `(visible: ChartSeries[]) => ReactNode` |  | Renders the chart with the series that are on. Colours stay stable. |
| `label` | `string` | `'Series'` | Accessible name for the group of toggles. |

## Example: Toggle series

```tsx
'use client';

import { ChartToggle, LineChart } from '@nexub/react';

const data = [
  { m: 'May', web: 120, ios: 80, android: 60 },
  { m: 'Jun', web: 140, ios: 95, android: 72 },
  { m: 'Jul', web: 150, ios: 110, android: 90 },
  { m: 'Aug', web: 170, ios: 128, android: 101 },
];
const series = [{ key: 'web', label: 'Web' }, { key: 'ios', label: 'iOS' }, { key: 'android', label: 'Android' }];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ChartToggle series={series} className="w-full">
      {(visible) => <LineChart legend={false} title="Signups by platform" data={data} index="m" series={visible} />}
    </ChartToggle>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- `Tab / Space`: Move between series and switch one on or off.
- Each series is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`. The last visible series cannot be switched off.

Related: [bar-chart](bar-chart.md), [line-chart](line-chart.md)

# Checkbox Card

A checkbox drawn as a whole card: title, description and optional icon. Pick any number.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form Controls · Status: beta
- Import: `import { CheckboxCard } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/checkbox-card

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The card’s accessible name. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Secondary text, exposed as the accessible description. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading icon. Turns primary when checked. |
| `checked / defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  | Controlled or initial state. No indeterminate state. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  | Called with a plain boolean. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content under the description. Keep it non-interactive. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the card. |

## Example: Features

Lay checkbox cards out with any grid; there is no group component.

```tsx
import { CheckboxCard } from '@nexub/react';
import { Bell, Shield, Zap } from '@nexub/icons';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <fieldset className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3 w-full border-0 p-0 m-0">
      <legend className="sr-only">Add-ons</legend>
      <CheckboxCard icon={<Bell />} title="Alerts" description="Email and push notifications." defaultChecked />
      <CheckboxCard icon={<Shield />} title="Audit log" description="Keep a year of activity." />
      <CheckboxCard icon={<Zap />} title="Automations" description="Run rules on new records." />
    </fieldset>
  );
}
```

## Example: Disabled

```tsx
import { CheckboxCard } from '@nexub/react';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-stretch w-[320px]">
      <CheckboxCard title="SSO" description="Available on Enterprise." disabled />
      <CheckboxCard title="Data residency" description="Included in your plan." defaultChecked disabled />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: checkbox
- `Tab`: Moves focus to the card.
- `Space`: Toggles the card.
- The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description.
- Wrap related cards in a `fieldset` with a `legend` so the set has a name.

Related: [checkbox](checkbox.md), [radio-card](radio-card.md), [card](card.md)
